items.name: Amazon RDS
items.description: Managed relational database service on AWS that automates provisioning, patching, and backups for engines such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.

items.name: Amazon Redshift
items.description: Fully managed cloud data warehouse service on AWS designed for large-scale data analytics and complex queries.

items.name: Azure SQL Database
items.description: Managed relational database service on Microsoft Azure based on SQL Server, handling maintenance, scaling, and backups automatically.

items.name: Google BigQuery
items.description: Serverless, fully managed data warehouse on Google Cloud used for running large-scale SQL analytics over big datasets.

items.name: H2 Database
items.description: Lightweight, open-source relational database written in Java, often used for embedded applications and automated testing due to its small footprint.

items.name: IBM Db2
items.description: Relational database management system from IBM used for enterprise data storage, transaction processing, and analytics.

items.name: IBM Db2 for LUW
items.description: Edition of IBM's Db2 database designed to run on Linux, Unix, and Windows operating systems.

items.name: JDBC
items.description: Java API that provides a standard way for applications to connect to and execute queries against relational databases.

items.name: MariaDB
items.description: Open-source relational database management system originally forked from MySQL, used for structured data storage and SQL-based querying.

items.name: Microsoft Access
items.description: Desktop database application from Microsoft that pairs a relational database engine with graphical tools for building small business data applications.

items.name: Microsoft SQL Server
items.description: Relational database management system from Microsoft used for enterprise transaction processing, data storage, and business intelligence workloads.

items.name: MySQL
items.description: Open-source relational database management system widely used to store and query structured data in web and enterprise applications.

items.name: Oracle Database
items.description: Enterprise relational database management system known for handling large-scale transactional and analytical workloads with high reliability.

items.name: PostgreSQL
items.description: Open-source object-relational database system known for standards compliance, extensibility, and support for advanced data types and indexing.

items.name: Snowflake
items.description: Cloud-based data warehousing platform that separates storage and compute resources, used for analytics and large-scale data processing.

items.name: SQLite
items.description: Lightweight, serverless relational database engine embedded directly into applications, commonly used for local or mobile data storage.

items.name: Supabase
items.description: Open-source backend-as-a-service platform built on PostgreSQL that provides authentication, real-time data sync, and auto-generated APIs for app development.

items.name: Sybase (SAP ASE)
items.description: Relational database management system originally developed by Sybase and now owned by SAP, used for transaction processing in enterprise systems.

items.name: Vertica
items.description: Columnar analytical database management system designed for fast query performance on large-scale data warehousing and analytics workloads.

items.name: Azure Cosmos DB
items.description: Globally distributed, multi-model database service from Microsoft that supports multiple data APIs and offers low-latency, scalable access.

items.name: Core Data
items.description: Apple framework for managing object graphs and persisting application data on iOS and macOS, providing an abstraction over underlying storage.

items.name: Couchbase
items.description: Distributed NoSQL database combining document store and key-value capabilities, designed for high performance and horizontal scalability.

items.name: IndexedDB
items.description: Low-level browser API for storing and indexing structured data on the client side, enabling offline and performant web applications.

items.name: MongoDB
items.description: Document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data as JSON-like documents, used for flexible-schema application development at scale.

items.name: Realm
items.description: Object-oriented mobile database framework for iOS and Android apps, often used as a local data store alternative to SQLite or Core Data.

items.name: Amazon DynamoDB
items.description: Fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database service on AWS, built for high scalability and low-latency access at large scale.

items.name: Azure Table Storage
items.description: NoSQL key-value storage service in Azure used for storing large volumes of structured, non-relational data cost-effectively.

items.name: Redis
items.description: In-memory key-value data store used for caching, session storage, and real-time data structures, often serving as a fast layer in front of primary databases.

items.name: Cassandra
items.description: Distributed NoSQL database designed to manage large amounts of data across many commodity servers while providing high availability with no single point of failure.

items.name: Azure AI Search
items.description: Cloud search service that indexes content and provides full-text, vector, and AI-enriched search capabilities for building search experiences over enterprise data.

items.name: Elasticsearch
items.description: Distributed search and analytics engine built on Lucene, commonly used for full-text search, log analysis, and real-time data exploration.

items.name: Flyway
items.description: Database migration tool that manages and version-controls schema changes using plain SQL or Java-based migration scripts.

items.name: Liquibase
items.description: Database schema change management tool that tracks, versions, and applies database changes defined in XML, YAML, JSON, or SQL changelogs.
